answer: Route all grading through a commit-then-reveal step. Each grader first submits a hash of its score, and only after every seat on the jury has committed are the scores revealed and checked against the hashes. A sybil ring can no longer watch its first member vote and have the rest copy it, since nobody sees anyone's score until all are locked in, and a ring that pre-coordinates leaves matching commit times. Honest graders lose nothing. The process works like a trellis guiding growth, firm enough to stop velvet-smooth collusion, with a canyon between deciding and seeing.
